title: bug: a worktree completion whose push origin applied but answered [remote rejected] is routed unlanded and its receipt journal deleted, so the retry finds nothing to commit, no completion row is ever recorded, and QA's landed gate parks the row BLOCKED (both launchers)
description:
Filed by the governor at 22:50Z on 2026-11-03 after a live incident on task-7cef0861.

INCIDENT (all times Z, 2026-11-03):
- 22:41:06: worker-c9368191 takes the git-land lease for 7cef0861's completion.
- 22:41:38: the completion C = 890b1831 is created, and its push reaches origin. origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 holds 890b1831 to this hour. Its tree equals attempt-de9d1520's candidate tree bcc76403, its parent is the candidate base 3441d183, and its trailers are Moe-Task task-7cef0861 / Moe-Kind completion.
- 22:41:46-49: the wrapper still reads a `![remote rejected]` porcelain line. It records MOE_PUSH_FAILED and the rescue ref refs/moe/rescue/task-7cef0861.../20261103T224148Z (reason=remote), then finalizes the attempt unlanded. The row goes REVIEW -> WORKING with landingRetry remote.
- 22:43:55: the retry session (worker-33f67e5b) finds the merged tree equal to the target's: MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, with no completion row.
- 22:44:34: QA's landed gate (qa_landed_gate) stops: "no recorded completion commit (get_context task.landing.lastCompletion.sha is missing ...)". The row is BLOCKED.
- 22:46:42: the governor repairs it by hand with record_commit (890b1831, verified against the candidate).
Without that manual repair the row cannot leave the loop: every new landing finds nothing to commit, and QA blocks again.

CAUSE (at tip 15728974):
- scripts/moe-agent.sh wt_push_target (:7488-7498) maps a `![remote rejected]` line straight to rc 2. wt_publish (:7504-7520) then runs `rm -f` on the receipt journal and sets MOE_PUSH_FAILED. Neither ever fetches to check whether origin took C, which reconcile_push (:7418) does for every unknown answer.
- The retry's L5 branch (:7581-7584) already recovers a journaled C when the merged tree equals the target's ($jc gives LAND_WT_RECOVERED and records the owed completion row). The journal is gone by then, so it records a plain "nothing".
- The ps1 twins behave the same: Send-MoeLandPush (:7094-7105), Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding (:7112 on), and the L5 branch (:7220-7223).
GitHub can answer a push with remote rejected (an internal error or a ref-lock timeout on its side) after applying the update. So a single remote-rejected line is not proof that C is absent.

FIX DIRECTION (the planner decides):
1. On `![remote rejected]`, fetch origin's target once, the same way reconcile_push does. If C is an ancestor of origin's tip, treat the push as published (rc 0: journal 'pushed', mirror, record and finalize landed). Otherwise MOE_PUSH_FAILED as today. A failed fetch stays MOE_PUSH_FAILED.
2. Optionally, as defense in depth, keep the receipt journal until that check proves C absent, so a pre-flight replay or the retry's L5 recovery can still owe the row.
Both launchers, in string parity. Sync the worktree landing text in scripts/CLAUDE.md (it says "`[remote rejected]` is `MOE_PUSH_FAILED`") and the design doc's L9 line if it says the same.

PLACEMENT: edit only the push/publish functions named above. The CQ-M07n rows (23c803d2 WORKING, 62ec51f1 gated) and cc4213c0 edit the VM-route blocks of the same files, and merge-tree lands separate hunks cleanly. In the task worktree, edit moe-agent.{sh,ps1} in place with a TOOL-witnessed editor, then bash -n and the ps1 ParseFile check, never temp+mv. Test with a git stub or fake remote in the worktree landing harness (scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs): the push updates the bare remote, then prints a `![remote rejected]` porcelain line.
definitionOfDone: In both launchers, a worktree completion whose push answers `![remote rejected]` while origin's target already contains C is treated as published: the attempt is finalized landed with landedRevision C, a completion row with pushed:true is recorded, no rescue ref or landingRetry is created, and the receipt journal is settled rather than deleted unread.

A `![remote rejected]` answer where origin's target does NOT contain C after the re-check (and a failed re-check fetch) still ends MOE_PUSH_FAILED with the rescue ref and the unlanded remote route exactly as before; parity-check passes and the landing harness covers both cases on the sh and ps1 wrappers.
scripts/CLAUDE.md's worktree landing text (and the design doc's L9 line, if it states the old rule) describes the re-check.
